'''Hugo Mario Krawczyk''' is an Argentine-Israeli cryptographer best known for co-inventing the [[HMAC]] message authentication algorithm and contributing in fundamental ways to the cryptographic architecture of central Internet standards, including [[IPsec]], [[Internet Key Exchange|IKE]], and [[Transport Layer Security|SSL/TLS]]. In particular, both IKEv2 and TLS 1.3 use Krawczyk's SIGMA protocol<ref>{{Cite book |last=Krawczyk |first=Hugo |title=Advances in Cryptology - CRYPTO 2003 |chapter=SIGMA: The 'SIGn-and-MAc' Approach to Authenticated Diffie-Hellman and its Use in the IKE Protocols |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |date=2003 |volume=2729 |chapter-url=https://webee.technion.ac.il/~hugo/sigma-pdf.pdf |pages=399–424 |doi=10.1007/978-3-540-45146-4_24 |isbn=978-3-540-40674-7 }}</ref> as the cryptographic core of their key exchange procedures.  He has also contributed foundational work in the areas of [[Threshold cryptosystem|threshold]] and [[Proactive secret sharing|proactive]] cryptosystems and [[searchable symmetric encryption]], among others.

==Education==
Krawczyk acquired a Bachelor of Arts in mathematics from the [[University of Haifa]]. Later he received his Master of Science and Ph.D. in computer science from [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology|Technion - Israel Institute of Technology]] with [[Oded Goldreich]] as doctoral thesis advisor.

==Career==
{{refimprove|section|date=April 2026}}
Hugo Krawczyk is a senior principal scientist at [[Amazon Web Services|Amazon Web Services (AWS)]]. Between 2019 and 2023 he was a Principal Researcher at the [[Algorand]] Foundation and part of its founding team. Prior to that, he was an [[IBM Fellow]] and Distinguished Research Staff Member at the [[IBM T.J. Watson Research Center]] in New York as  a member of the Cryptography Research group from 1992 to 1997, and again from 2004 to 2019. He was  an associate professor at the [[Technion Faculty of Electrical Engineering|Department of Electrical Engineering at the Technion]] in Israel from 1997 until 2004.

Krawczyk has published over 100 papers with [https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=-coqiSIAAAAJ more than 35,000 citations], and is an inventor in 30 issued patents.

His research includes both theoretical and applied elements of cryptography, with a focus on internet security, privacy, and authentication. His most recent projects in the area include: [[Transport Layer Security|TLS]] 1.3, the new-generation SSL/TLS;  [[HKDF]], the standard for key derivation embraced by TLS 1.3, [[Signal (messaging app)|Signal]], [[WhatsApp]], [[Facebook Messenger]], and others; and [[Password-authenticated key agreement|OPAQUE]], a password authentication protocol being standardized by the [[Internet Research Task Force|IRTF]] and recently  deployed by Facebook in its implementation of end-to-end encrypted chat backups for WhatsApp.<ref name="facebook">{{citation | title= Whatsapp e2e | url= https://engineering.fb.com/2021/09/10/security/whatsapp-e2ee-backups/}}</ref>

Krawczyk is the author of many other cryptographic algorithms and protocols including the [[MQV|HMQV]] key-exchange protocol, the LFSR-based [[Toeplitz Hash Algorithm]], the [[Shrinking generator|Shrinking Generator]] encryption scheme, the [[UMAC (cryptography)|UMAC]] message authentication code, and the [[Cryptographic hash function|randomized hashing]] scheme for strengthening digital signatures.
 
Other influential work includes [[Threshold cryptosystem|threshold]] and [[Proactive secret sharing|proactive]] cryptosystems (including [[distributed key generation]]), [[searchable symmetric encryption]],  and theoretical contributions to secure cryptographic communications, password protocols, zero knowledge and pseudorandomness.

==Awards==
Krawczyk, a [[International Association for Cryptologic Research|Fellow of the International Association of Cryptologic Research (IACR)]] and 2017 [[IBM Fellow]],  has won the [[RSA Award for Excellence in Mathematics|RSA Conference Award for Excellence in Mathematics]] in 2015, the [[Levchin Prize]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Levchin Prize for Real-World Cryptography |url=https://rwc.iacr.org/LevchinPrize/ |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=rwc.iacr.org}}</ref> for Contributions to Real-World Cryptography in 2018, the [[Paris Kanellakis Award|ACM Paris Kanellakis Theory and Practice Award]] in 2025,<ref>{{Cite web |title=ACM Paris Kanellakis Award |url=https://awards.acm.org/kanellakis |website=ACM Paris Kanellakis Award}}</ref> and two IBM corporate awards (2005 and 2008). He is the recipient of two Test-of-Time awards: In 2019 for his 1996 NDSS paper,<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Donoghue |first=Karen |date=2019-02-28 |title=NDSS 2019 Honors Timeless Papers |url=https://www.internetsociety.org/blog/2019/02/ndss-2019-honors-timeless-papers/ |access-date=2022-11-15 |website=Internet Society |language=en-US}}</ref> “SKEME: A versatile secure key exchange mechanism for internet”, a precursor of KEM-based key exchange protocols, central to developing post-quantum key exchange standards, and in 2025 for his CRYPTO 2010 "Cryptographic Extraction and Key Derivation: The HKDF Scheme" paper "for formalizing key derivation and introducing HKDF, a widely adopted and standardized extract-then-expand scheme."<ref>{{Cite web |title=IACR Test-of-Time Award |url=https://www.iacr.org/testoftime/}}</ref>
